t: Prayers for Yom Tov – Prayer Before Retiring at Night

items.n: Prayers for Yom Tov:Blessings on the Lulav
items.e: Many recite the following prayer before taking the four species (Lulav).
our God, King of the Universe
Who sanctified us with His commandments
concerning the taking of the lulav.
If you are taking the lulav for the first time on Sukkos, you should also recite:
our God, King of the Universe
Who has kept us alive and sustained us
and brought us to this time.
Prayers Said Upon Entering the Sukkah
in the shade of the Holy One, blessed is He.
Behold, I am prepared and ready
to perform the mitzvah [to sit in the] sukkah,
as I was commanded by the Creator,
“In sukkos you shall dwell seven days;
in order that your generations may know
I caused the Children of Israel to dwell
when I took them out of the land of Egypt.”
Be seated, be seated, esteemed guests,
be seated, be seated, holy guests,
of the Holy One, blessed is He.
and worthy is the portion of Israel,
Jacob, the lot of His inheritance.”
For the sake of the unity
of the Holy One, blessed is He,
to unify the Name Yud-Kay with Vov-Kay
through Him Who is Most Hidden,
in the name of all Israel.
May the pleasantness of my Master, our God,
and the work of our hands establish for us;
and the work of our hands may He establish.
Adonoy, our God, and the God of our fathers,
to cause Your Presence to dwell among us;
and spread over us the shelter of Your peace
in the merit of the mitzvah of sukkah
that we are performing, to unify the Name of
the Holy One, blessed is He and His Presence,
with reverence and love, to unify the Name
Yud-Kay with Vov-Kay in complete unity,
in the name of all Israel;
with the splendor of Your honor,
spread over their [our] heads from above
as an eagle arousing its nestlings;
bountiful outpourings of life for Your servant
And in the merit of my leaving my house, to go out [into the sukkah],
and the path of Your commandments,
may this be considered for me
as though I have wandered far off [in exile].
Cleanse me thoroughly from my iniquity,
and from my sin, purify me.
give them their food and their water
in the sheltering shadow of Your wings—
at the time I leave this world—
to take refuge from the stream [of fire]
and from the rain [of fiery coals]
when You rain snare-traps upon the wicked.
the mitzvah of sukkah that I perform—
as though I had fulfilled it
in all its particulars, exactness, specifications,
and all the mitzvos dependent on it.
May it be for our good when You seal [the judgements of Rosh Hashanah —Yom Kippur,]
to dwell many days upon the land,
in Your service and in Your reverence.
Blessed is Adonoy forever, amein and amein.
may there be seated with me and with you—
may there be seated with me and with you—
may there be seated with me and with you—
may there be seated with me and with you—
may there be seated with me and with you—
may there be seated with me and with you—
may there be seated with me and with you—
this mitzvah of sitting in the sukkah
as though I had fulfilled it
in all of its particulars and exactness,
and the six hundred thirteen mitzvos
as though I had in mind
by the Men of the Great Assembly.

items.n: Prayers for Yom Tov:Kiddush for Yom Tov Evenings
items.e: When Yom Tov occurs on Shabbos, begin here:
And evening came, then morning came,
And the heavens and the earth were completed
And God completed, by the seventh day,
His work which He had done;
and He abstained on the seventh day
from all His work which He had done.
And God blessed the seventh day
which God had created to do.
Attention! Our masters and our teachers
our God, King of the Universe,
Creator of the fruit of the vine.
our God, King of the Universe,
Who takes bread out from the earth.
our God, King of the Universe
Who chose us from among all peoples,
and exalted us above all (tongues) languages,
and sanctified us with His commandments.
And [You] gave us Adonoy, our God,
the season of the giving of our Torah,
On Shemini Atseres and Simchas Torah
and Your appointed festivals of holiness
You gave us for a heritage.
On the first night of Sukkos, the berachah לישב בסוכה , (p. 000) is recited before the following berachah. On the second night, the berachos are said in the sequence as printed.
(On the last two nights of Pesach the following berachah is omitted)
our God, King of the Universe
Who has kept us alive and sustained us
and brought us to this season.
our God, King of the Universe
Who sanctified us with His commandments
and commanded us to dwell in the Sukkah.
(When Yom Tov occurs at the conclusion of Shabbos, the following two berachos are said before the berachah of “ שֶׁהֶחֱיָנוּ , Who has kept us alive”):
our God, King of the Universe,
Creator of the lights of fire.
our God, King of the Universe,
between the sacred and the unhallowed,
and the sanctity of Yom Tov
[from] the six work days You have sanctified.
Your people Israel with Your holiness.
Who distinguished between sacred and sacred.

items.n: Prayers for Yom Tov:Amidah for Yom Tov Maariv, Shacharis and Minchah

items.e: At Maariv and Shacharis, begin here:
and my mouth will declare Your praise.
our God, and God of our fathers,
God of Abraham, God of Isaac,
the Great, the Powerful, the Awesome,
Who remembers the piety of the Patriarchs,
for the sake of His Name, with love.
King, Helper, and Deliverer and Shield.
You are mighty forever, my Master;
You are the Resurrector of the dead
the powerful One to deliver us.
(On Pesach except for Shacharis of the first day, on Shavuos and Sukkos including Shacharis of Shemini Atzeres say:
He causes the dew to descend.
(From Mincha of Shemini Atzeres until after Shacharis on the first day of Pesach say:
Causer of the wind to blow
and of the rain to fall.)
If you forgot to say this, see page 000.
Sustainer of the living with kindliness,
Resurrector of the dead with great mercy,
to those who sleep in the dust.
Who is like You, Master of mighty deeds,
and who can be compared to You?
King Who causes death and restores life,
and causes deliverance to sprout forth.
to restore the dead to life.
When praying silently, continue “You are holy” on page 000.
When the Chazzan repeats the Shemoneh Esrei during Shacharis, the Kedushah is said here. For Mincha turn to page 000.
The Congregation says and the Chazzan repeats:
We will hallow and revere You
of the company of the holy Seraphim
as is written by the hand of Your prophet,
“And they called to one another and said:
the fullness of all the earth is His glory.'”
Facing them, they offer praise and say:
Then, with the sound of great rushing,
raising themselves up toward the Serafim,
Facing them, they offer praise and say:
From Your place, our King, You will appear
When will You reign in Zion?
You will be exalted and sanctified
for all generations and for all eternity.
May our eyes behold Your kingship,
as it is said in the songs of Your might
Your God, Zion, throughout all generations!
The Congregation says and the Chazzan repeats:
We will hallow and revere You
of the company of the holy Seraphim
as is written by the hand of Your prophet,
“And they called one to another, and said:
the fullness of all the earth is His glory.'”
Facing them, they offer praise and say:
And in Your Holy Words it is written:
Your God, Zion, throughout all generations!
You are holy and Your Name is holy
For a great and Almighty King—
You chose us from [among] all the peoples;
You loved us and took pleasure in us;
You exalted us above all tongues,
You drew us near, our King, to Your servitude,
and Your great and holy Name
When the Festival falls on Motzoei Shabbos say:
You have made known to us, Adonoy, our God,
and have taught us to perform
And [You] gave us, Adonoy our God,
upright judgments and teachings of truth,
statutes and commandments that are good.
You have given us as a heritage
and the feasts of the pilgrimage festival.
between the sacred and the unhallowed,
and the sanctity of Yom Tov
[from] the six work days You have sanctified.
Your people Israel with Your holiness.
And [You] gave us Adonoy, our God,
the season of the giving of the Torah,
On Shemini Atseres and Simchas Torah:
Our God and God of our fathers,
may there ascend, come, and reach,
the son of David, Your servant;
and the remembrance of Your entire people,
the House of Israel, before You
be mindful of us on this day for blessing,
and deliver us for good life.
In accord with the promise of deliverance
have compassion on us and deliver us;
for to You our eyes are directed
Who is King, Gracious and Merciful.
with the blessing of Your appointed seasons
and You promised to bless us.
Our God and God of our fathers:
and give us a share in Your Torah,
and gladden our souls with Your deliverance,
and purify our hearts to serve You in truth,
and give us as a heritage, Adonoy, our God,
and may Israel rejoice in You—
[they who are] sanctifiers of Your Name.
with Your people Israel and their prayer,
to the Holy of Holies in Your abode,
and accept their prayer, lovingly and willingly.
And may You always find pleasure
with the service of Your people, Israel.
Who returns His Divine Presence to Zion.
At the words,We are thankful, bend forward; at Adonoy return to an upright position.
that You Adonoy are our God
and the God of our fathers forever;
our Rock, Rock of our lives,
We will give thanks to You
which are committed into Your hand.
And for our souls which are entrusted to You,
and for Your miracles of every day with us
and for Your wonders and benefactions
for Your compassion is never withheld;
we have always placed our hope in You.
(When the Chazzan repeats the Shemoneh Esrei and says, “Who returns His Divine Presence to Zion”, the congregation responds by saying “Amein” and then the following prayer. )
that You Adonoy are our God
Our Creator, Creator of the Beginning.
to Your great and holy Name
for keeping us alive, and sustaining us;
so may You always keep us alive
to the Courtyards of Your Sanctuary
for we are thankful to You.
to Whom all thanks are due.
And all the living shall thank You forever
Your great Name with sincerity forever;
the Almighty, Who is our deliverance
and You it is fitting to praise.
To be said by the Chazzan at Shacharis Priestly Blessings
Our God, and God of our fathers, bless us
with the threefold blessing of the Torah,
written by the hand of Moses, Your servant,
pronounced from the mouth of Aaron
and his sons, the kohanim, Your holy people;
Adonoy bless you and guard you.
Adonoy shine His countenance upon you
Adonoy turn His countenance toward you
upon us and upon all Israel, Your people.
Bless us, our Father, all of us as one
with the light of Your countenance.
For by the light of Your countenance
You gave us Adonoy our God,
a Torah of life and the love of kindliness,
And may it be good in Your sight
and to bless Your people Israel,
at all times and at every moment

are the Master of all peace.
And may it be good in Your sight
and to bless Your people Israel,
at all times and at every moment
and the thoughts of my heart, before You
Adonoy, my Rock and my Redeemer.
My God, guard my tongue from evil
and my lips from speaking deceitfully.
and let my soul be like dust to all.
Open my heart to Your Torah
and let my soul pursue Your commandments.
And all who plan evil against me,
Adonoy, my God and God of my fathers,
that no person be envious of me
and that I not be envious of others,
that I not be brought to anger this day,
and that I not cause Your anger;
and save me from the evil inclination,
and help me be humble and any modest.
unify Your Name in Your world,
rebuild Your city, establish Your house
redeem Your people, rejoice Your congregation).
Act for the sake of Your Name.
Act for the sake of Your right hand.
Act for the sake of Your Torah.
Act for the sake of Your holiness.
In order that Your loved ones be released,
deliver [with] Your right hand and answer me.

and the thoughts of my heart—before You
Adonoy, my Rock and my Redeemer.
upon us and upon all Israel
Adonoy, our God, and the God of our Fathers
that the Holy Temple be rebuilt
and grant us our share in Your Torah.
And there we will serve You reverently
as in the days of old,
with the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem
as in the days of old and in earlier years.
At the Minchah and Maariv services, the Chazzan recites the Whole Kaddish on page 000. The congregation says עָלֵינוּ on page 000, and mourners recite Kaddish on page 000.

On the first two nights of Pesach, some congregations recite הַלֵל on page 000, and then continue as above. On the second night of Pesach, the Counting of the Omer, page 000, is said, and then continue עָלֵינוּ as above.
On Sukkos, לְדָוִד ה' , page 000, is said after עָלֵינוּ .
On Friday night, וַיְכֻלוּ , page 000 is recited before the Chazzan recites the Whole Kaddish.
At Shacharis, הַלֵל , page 000, is said. The Chazzan then recites the Whole Kaddish, and the service continues with the Order of the Reading of the Torah on page 000.
In most synagogues, the Chazzan chants this song after the Haftorah blessings are said. On Yom Tov days when Yizkor is recied this piyut is usually omitted.
Memorial Service for the Souls of the Departed
On the last day of Pesach, the second day of Shavuos, on Yom Kippur, and on Shemini Atseres, the Yizkor prayer in memory of the departed, is said following the Reading of the Torah.
the soul of my father, my teacher,
(Mention his Hebrew name and that of his father)
who has gone to his world,
I pledge [without vowing] to donate charity
In this merit, may his soul
be bound up in the bond of life,
and with the other righteous men and women
who are in the Gan Eiden (Paradise)
the soul of my mother, my teacher,
(Mention her Hebrew name and that of her father)
who has gone to her world.
I pledge [without vowing] to donate charity
In this merit, may her soul
be bound up in the bond of life,
and with the other righteous men and women
May God remember the soul of my
who have gone to their world,
I pledge [without vowing] to donate charity
In this merit may their soul
be bound up in the bond of life,
and with the other righteous men and women
for the sanctification of Your Name,
I pledge [without vowing] to donate charity
for the sake of their memories.
In this merit, may their souls
be bound up in the bond of life,
and with the other righteous men and women
Who dwells on the highest heights,
on the wings of [Your] Divine Presence,
in the exalted spheres of the holy and pure
who shine like the brightness of the firmament,
(Mention the name of the deceased and that of his father)
who has gone to his world,
in the shelter of His wings, forever,
his soul with the bond of eternal life.
and may he rest in his repose in peace,
Who dwells on the highest heights
on the wings of [Your] Divine Presence,
in the exalted spheres of the holy and the pure
who shine like the brightness of the firmament,
(mention the name of the deceased and that of her father)
who has gone to her world,
in the shelter of His wings, forever,
her soul with the bond of life.
and may she rest in her repose in peace,
At the conclusion of Yizkor, Av Horachamim (page 000) is said.

items.e: Even though the kohanim are commanded to bless Israel every day (according to some authorities) nevertheless, the custom outside the Holy Land is that koha- nim bless the people only during the Musaf Service of the Festivals, and the High Holidays. One reason given is that the Priestly Blessings are pronounced only in a festive atmosphere. Thus on weekdays when people are troubled with the difficul- ties of earning a livelihood, and even on the Sabbath when people are disturbed by thoughts of their economic plight, the blessings are not pronounced.
During the Musaf Service of the Festivals, however, which precedes the festive meal of the holiday, a joyous atmosphere does prevail and the Priestly Blessing is pronounced.

The Omer is counted from the second night of Passover until the night before Shavuos. The counting of forty-nine days (seven weeks) between the Festival of Passover and Shavuos (the Feast of Weeks), connects the exodus from Egypt with the festival of the giving of the Torah. Just as one who awaits a most intimate friend on a certain day counts the days in eager anticipation of his arrival, so do we count the days from our liberation till the day we receive the Torah, which is the culmination and fulfillment of our freedom.
It is proper to count the Omer at the beginning of the night, usually after the Maariv Service, and the Omer should be counted while standing.
